subject: Temporary throughput uplift for go-live - LuminaHealth
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@luminahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@luminahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary throughput uplift for go-live - LuminaHealth

Hi Rishi,

We’re ramping up for our July 20 go-live for the new patient intake flow and expect an initial traffic spike that will materially exceed our normal baseline. Early load testing shows short bursts up to ~2,000 req/s (our current Redwood baseline quota is 500 req/s). The burst pattern is highly spiky during the first 48–72 hours as users land and complete signups.

Can Redwood support a temporary uplift to accommodate that spike (preferably starting 00:00 UTC on Jul 20) and provide clarity on how that interacts with the existing rate-limit fairness policy and any latency SLA commitments? Specifically:
- Can we get a temporary quota increase for the LuminaHealth project for 72 hours?
- During that window, will Redwood give any prioritized routing / reduced throttling to avoid client-facing 429s?
- If there are additional costs or credits associated with a one-off uplift, what do those look like?

I attached a small traffic sample from our load tests (traffic-sample-July15.csv) to help size the uplift.

We’d like to get agreement this week so we can lock deployment times.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
LuminaHealth

Attachment: traffic-sample-July15.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput uplift for go-live - LuminaHealth

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads up and for the sample. Short answers: we can support a temporary uplift, but we need to align on exact numbers, the SLO implications, and the operational runbook (on-call coverage, monitoring hooks, rollback plan).

Can you confirm:
- Which project ID / API key will be used for the go-live?
- Expected sustained vs burst (peak) in requests/sec and tokens/sec across the 72-hour window (the sample is helpful but we need expected production numbers).

I’ve looped in Marissa (sales/solutions) and Vivek (ops) — they’ll propose the recommended config and any required paperwork (amendment / DocuSign). I’ll coordinate approvals on our side once we have the numbers.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput uplift for go-live - LuminaHealth

Hi Samantha / Rishi — reviewed the sample and did a quick sizing pass with ops. Recommendations below (operational, not a permanent SLA change):

Summary proposal
- Temporary quota increase: bump LuminaHealth project from 500 req/s baseline to 1,500 req/s sustained, with short bursts allowed to 2,200 req/s for 10s windows for the first 72 hours starting at your chosen go-live time.
- Fairness & throttling policy: we will place LuminaHealth in a "preferential routing" bucket for the 72-hour window. That means: reduced soft-throttling thresholds and routing through a dedicated burst pool; hard throttles remain in place for abusive sustained traffic.
- Latency SLO: Our standard latency SLA (p50/p95 targets) remains unchanged in contract terms. We cannot extend contractual latency guarantees for temporary traffic beyond what’s covered by the service agreement, but we will prioritize routing and monitoring to minimize client-visible degradation and provide post-mortem metrics.
- Cost/credits: we propose pro-rated usage billing for the uplift window at the normal on-demand rates and a goodwill credit of one week of hosted usage applied to your next invoice given this is a one-off start-of-life event.
- Runbook: ops will create an OPS ticket and assign on-call coverage for Jul 20–23 with automated alerts to your SRE and ours.

Next steps we need from Lumina:
1) Confirm exact go-live UTC start time.
2) Confirm project ID / API key to which the uplift applies.
3) Sign a short amendment (attached: SLA-Amendment-Lumina-draft.pdf) authorizing the temporary quota changes and confirming billing treatment.

I’ve attached a draft amendment for signature. Vivek — can you please spin up the OPS ticket (OPS-4821) and note time window once Samantha confirms?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-Amendment-Lumina-draft.pdf (PDF, 12 KB)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@luminahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@luminahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary throughput uplift for go-live - LuminaHealth

Thanks Marissa — that all sounds reasonable. We confirm:
- Go-live window start: 2026-07-20 00:00 UTC (target) for 72 hours.
- Project ID: lumina-prod-123 (API key will be sent to the ops contact direct).

We accept the proposed temporary quota (1,500 req/s sustained, 2,200 req/s short bursts) and the one-week goodwill credit. Please send the amendment for signature and we’ll return signed by EOD tomorrow.

Also: can you add a short clause in the amendment saying Redwood will provide a post-mortem with latency/availability metrics for the 72-hour window? That would help our internal compliance folks.

Samantha
